short: Proc macros for the application layer
is: The workspace's one proc-macro crate: `#[use_case]` (dependency injection + the unit-of-work bracket around a use-case method) and `#[derive(WithPorts)]` (the ports-bag plumbing of a use-case namespace), both consumed only by `application`.
conventions: One file per macro under `src/`, each exposing a `pub(crate) fn expand_*(…) -> syn::Result<TokenStream>`; `lib.rs` holds only the `#[proc_macro_*]` entry points and turns an `Err` into `compile_error!`.
Emitted code names its targets as `crate::…` (`crate::ports::WithPorts`, `crate::Ports`), so both macros only expand correctly inside `application`.
Bad input is a spanned `syn::Error` on the offending token, never a panic.

fs.name: Cargo.toml
fs.role: proc-macro = true; deps proc-macro2 + quote + syn(full); dev-dep trybuild (no tests/ui yet)

fs.name: src/lib.rs
fs.role: the two entry points: `#[use_case]` attribute, `#[derive(WithPorts)]` with its `#[ports]` helper attribute

fs.name: src/use_case.rs
fs.role: splits an async `&self` method into `<name>_inner_injected` (the body, all params) and a same-named wrapper without the `#[ports]`/`#[unit]` params; with `#[unit]` the wrapper begins a unit, commits on `Ok`, rolls back on `Err`

fs.name: src/with_ports.rs
fs.role: derives `WithPorts` from the single `#[ports]` field: a child (`&'a Parent<'a>`) delegates to its parent and the parent gains a lowercased accessor building the child; `#[ports(is_root = true)]` returns the field itself and emits no accessor

refs.title: Transactions as a capability — a compile-enforced Unit of Work in the private store
refs.governs: src/use_case.rs: the generated wrapper is the begin/commit/rollback bracket of a use case

refs.title: The Application Layer — Use Cases, DTOs and Ports
refs.governs: src/use_case.rs + src/with_ports.rs: the shape of a use-case method and of the namespaces that carry the Ports bag

notes: The wrapper's own `begin`/`commit`/`rollback` calls carry `#[allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)]`; `application/clippy.toml` bans those three methods everywhere else in that crate.
A `#[use_case]` must inject at least one of `#[ports]`/`#[unit]` and needs a `self` receiver, so free functions and bodies that touch neither stay plain fns.
The inner fn keeps the outer fn's visibility and attributes.
The derive's child form builds the struct from the parent field alone, so a child namespace cannot carry extra fields; a root can.
